tells: 1. The laugh never builds: across the six frames (1.0 s) only the white-sweater woman raises her hand to her chin and the pink-jacket man turns his head. Purple top, blonde, teal hoodie and the back tables hold the same pose and expression throughout, so it reads as one person reacting, not a room (club-5-strip.png, whole frame, front table pair right of centre)

2. Front row is a pose catalogue: five of the six front sitters have both forearms flat on the table with hands clasped round the candle in near-identical symmetric postures, all upright and facing camera, like a lineup rather than people at drinks (club-1-wide.png, front row centre and right tables)

3. Repeated identities are easy to spot at TV distance: the same blonde-bun woman shows up twice in the second row and the teal-hoodie, pink-jacket and white-sweater characters appear in every shot in the same seats and clothes (club-2-mid.png, left second row; club-3-mid.png, centre)

4. Face close is waxy and glassy-eyed: the cheek and forehead shading is flat, the eyes have no wet highlight or focus, the hand-to-chin gesture sits on the jaw with fingers splayed stiffly, and the defocused blonde behind has a hard cut-out neck edge (club-4-face.png, centre face and hand; left background figure)

5. Back of house is a band of dark standing silhouettes at uniform height with no motion between frames, plus a rim-lit figure cut against the bright bar sign, so the depth reads as cardboard (club-1-wide.png, upper middle band and bar sign at right of centre)

1. Front row sits bolt upright with arms hanging straight down and hands resting on the knees in near-identical mannequin poses, all facing camera, and the second tier does the same. It reads as a lineup or a casting photo, not an audience settled into theatre seats (theatre-1-wide.png, front two rows centre)

2. Upper tiers are flat, motionless cut-out silhouettes with identical shoulder lines and no head or shoulder variation between strip frames: a visible impostor wall behind the lit rows (theatre-1-wide.png, top half; theatre-5-strip.png, upper band)

3. Shading and texture faults on the lit side: a grey-white slab torso with no folds on the second-row man, a woman's bare arm rendered as a flat grey tube with a hard edge, and several faces on the left tier that look pasted on (theatre-6-held.png, left edge at x~80,y~420 and x~200,y~600)

4. Front-row legs stick out stiffly from the seats with little thigh compression, and some bodies look perched on the seat edge rather than sitting into it. The leftmost front sitters' legs come off the seat line (theatre-3-mid.png, front row left, x~300-450)

5. The laugh comes late and in pieces: through 12.0-12.4 nobody changes, then at 12.6-12.8 three or four mouths open together and the teal-hoodie man drops his head at 13.0, with no ripple outward from one first laugher. The open-mouth close has teeth and a hand set like a still pose, and the eyes don't squint (theatre-5-strip.png, front row; theatre-4-face.png, eyes and hand)

1. Wide shows a slumped clone posture: nearly every front sitter leans forward with forearms hanging between the knees and hands together, the same silhouette repeated about ten times shoulder to shoulder (openmic-1-wide.png, front row full width)

2. Hair is alpha-hashed: the yellow-shirt man's hair edge is a dithered, stippled card with a hard boundary against the background, very visible in the close and shimmering in the mids (openmic-4-face.png, top right of head; openmic-2-mid.png, yellow-shirt man)

3. Bodies interpenetrate in the packed row: the yellow-shirt man's shoulder sinks into the green-top woman, the dark-hoodie woman's arm clips the green-top woman's arm, and the hand contact in the laugh passes through a sleeve (openmic-3-mid.png, centre; openmic-5-strip.png, t=13.0 centre)

4. Laugh faces are grimaces: wide rectangular mouths with flat lips and full teeth, the eyes don't squint and the cheeks don't rise, so the dark-hoodie woman and the bun blonde read as shouting or pained rather than laughing (openmic-2-mid.png, centre-right faces)

5. The lean into the laugh is a big pose snap: the dark-hoodie woman goes from upright to a deep forward crouch within 0.2 s between 12.4 and 12.6, and the red-jacket man at the end stands rigid with his hands in his pockets throughout, with no breathing or weight shift (openmic-5-strip.png, t=12.4 to 12.6 right of centre; openmic-3-mid.png, right edge)
